chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn [Ali ibn] al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl ibn Ja'far ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Sulayman ibn Abdullah ibn al-Abbas narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Za'farani al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Talaqani narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah, the mawla of the Banu Hashim, narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Waqidi, from al-Hudhail, from al-Makhul, from al-Tabus, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him):

When Allah, Exalted and Glorious be His remembrance, created Adam and blew into him from His Spirit, and made His angels prostrate to him, and settled him in His Garden, and married him to Hawwa' (his wife), he raised his gaze towards the Throne and saw five lines written. Adam said: 'O Lord, who are these?' Allah, Exalted and Glorious, said to him: 'These are those whom if My creation intercede with, I will intercede for them.' Adam said: 'O Lord, by their position with You, what are their names?' He, Exalted, said: 'As for the first, I am the Praised and he is Muhammad; and the second, I am the High and he is Ali; and the third, I am the Splitter and she is Fatima; and the fourth, I am the Beneficent and he is al-Hasan; and the fifth, I am the One with Good Deeds and he is al-Husayn.' All of them praise Allah, Exalted and Glorious.
ai.seo_question: What are the five names written on the Throne in the vision of Adam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* presents a cosmological narrative where Adam witnesses the 'Ahl al-Bayt' inscribed on the Divine Throne, linking their identities to specific divine attributes like Al-Mahmud (The Praiseworthy) and Al-Ali (The Exalted). In Shia scholarship, this establishes the ontological precedence of the Imams, portraying them not merely as historical figures but as eternal realities integral to God’s self-disclosure and intercessory role. The text reinforces the concept of *Tawassul* by illustrating how these five figures serve as the primary means through which creation seeks divine favor.
